descriptors.concept_name: Initial Measurement Factors for Assets and Liabilities
descriptors.definition: Initial measurement evaluates an asset or liability at recognition, typically matching its subsequent measurement basis. Market transactions generally equate initial cost to fair value unless transaction costs are material.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from off-market transactions where terms are influenced by related parties or special conditions.

descriptors.definition: Market transactions involve cash or equivalent exchanges where initial cost aligns closely with fair value. Exchanges of assets or liabilities determine whether income or expense arises based on carrying versus fair values.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike off-market transactions, market terms reflect standard fair value equivalencies without concessions.

descriptors.concept_name: Transactions Not on Market Terms (Off-Market Transactions)
descriptors.definition: Off-market transactions occur outside standard commercial terms, such as through related-party relationships or government grants. Such events require measurement at deemed cost or fair value, recognizing differences as income, expenses, or equity contributions.
inclusion: government grants of assets free of charge
exclusion: cash transactions on standard market terms
nearby_distinctions: Unlike market transactions, off-market transactions necessitate adjustments like equity contributions when consideration differs from fair value.

descriptors.definition: Multiple measurement bases may be necessary when using a single basis fails to faithfully represent both financial position and performance. Total current value changes can be separated so that profit or loss reflects one basis while other comprehensive income captures the remainder.
inclusion: interest-bearing financial assets measured at fair value through OCI
separation of total fair value changes
exclusion: single measurement basis applied uniformly without separation
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from single-basis reporting by segregating performance impacts between profit or loss and OCI.

descriptors.definition: Total equity is determined residually as the difference between recognized assets and liabilities rather than measured directly. Financial statements do not represent the entity's aggregate market value or enterprise sale price.
inclusion: direct measurement of specific equity components
exclusion: aggregate market value of equity claims
nearby_distinctions: Unlike assets and liabilities that may have direct measurement bases, total equity is always calculated residually.

descriptors.concept_name: Presentation and Disclosure Objectives and Principles
descriptors.definition: Financial statement communication balances entity flexibility with cross-period and cross-entity comparability. Effective reporting prioritizes entity-specific information while avoiding unnecessary duplication.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on communication principles rather than recognition or measurement criteria.

descriptors.definition: Classification categorizes financial statement elements based on shared characteristics such as nature, business function, or measurement basis. Grouping dissimilar items obscures relevant information and reduces understandability.
inclusion: sorting income and expenses by shared traits
nearby_distinctions: Differs from aggregation, which combines items already sharing the same classification.

descriptors.definition: Classification applies primarily to selected units of account for assets and liabilities, separating components when differing characteristics warrant it. Separating current and non-current components enhances the utility of financial information.
inclusion: separating asset components by maturity or characteristic
current and non-current balance sheet segregation
exclusion: offsetting separate asset and liability units into a single net total
nearby_distinctions: Applies classification rules to distinct asset and liability components rather than treating sets of rights as single units.

descriptors.definition: Offsetting combines separately recognized assets and liabilities into a single net balance sheet amount. Because this practice groups dissimilar items, it is generally inappropriate unless specifically permitted.
inclusion: combining separate asset and liability units into a single net figure
exclusion: treating a single set of rights and obligations as one unit of account
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from treating a single contractual set of rights and obligations as a single unit of account.

descriptors.definition: Equity claims and components are classified separately when they possess distinct characteristics or face specific regulatory constraints. Separate presentation helps identify reserves subject to legal distribution restrictions.
inclusion: separate classification of equity claims with different characteristics
exclusion: aggregating all equity claims into a single undifferentiated pool
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on legal and structural distinctions among equity claims rather than asset classification.

descriptors.definition: Income and expenses are classified based on the underlying unit of account or separated components possessing different characteristics. Separating distinct components like value changes and interest accrual enhances reporting usefulness.
inclusion: separating interest accrual from value changes
exclusion: lumping distinct revenue and expense components without structural basis
nearby_distinctions: Applies classification criteria to financial performance flows rather than balance sheet positions.

descriptors.concept_name: Profit or Loss and Other Comprehensive Income
descriptors.definition: All income and expenses are included in profit or loss unless exceptional standard-setting permits inclusion in other comprehensive income. Items in other comprehensive income may subsequently be reclassified into profit or loss when relevant.
inclusion: inclusion of performance items in profit or loss
exceptional allocation of current value changes to other comprehensive income
exclusion: permanent omission of performance items from financial statements
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes primary performance reporting in profit or loss from items routed through other comprehensive income.
